title: Structural Function
learningObjectives: Explain the armature's structural and visual roles.
student: Why does the mounted tail require a concealed structural armature?
instructor: The armature supports the mounted tail elements, carries their gravity loads to the main frame, and remains visually unobtrusive so it does not distract from the skeleton.

title: Gravity Loads
learningObjectives: Interpret the assigned total distributed load.
student: Identify the gravity loads and explain how they reach the armature. Is the assigned intensity defined per horizontal length or per arc length?
instructor: Vertebrae and cradle loads pass into the armature along with steel self-weight. The assigned total intensity includes both and is defined per meter of arc length.

title: Root Restraint
student: Identify the idealized root restraint and its restrained planar degrees of freedom.
instructor: The equivalent fixed root restrains horizontal and vertical translation and in-plane rotation.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace load transfer to the building.
student: Trace the load path from the vertebra cradles through the support system to the floor.
instructor: Vertebrae and cradles → curved armature → pelvis/main mounting frame → base support → floor/building structure.

title: Critical Region
student: Predict where bending stress is likely to be greatest and justify your prediction before calculating.
instructor: The fixed root is expected to govern because all outboard gravity load contributes moment there.

title: Local Axial Force
learningObjectives: Relate global gravity force to local resultants.
student: Why can a purely vertical external load produce a nonzero axial force at an inclined curved-member cut?
instructor: The vertical section force has components along both the local tangent and local normal at an inclined cut; its tangential component is the local axial resultant.

title: Required Properties
learningObjectives: Identify inputs for the strength check.
student: Identify the geometric and material properties required for the proposed normal-stress and yield-margin check.
instructor: Required inputs include the arc geometry and cut location, load-intensity function, tube dimensions and design thickness, area, strong-axis inertia and extreme-fiber distance, yield strength, and required safety factor.

title: Student-Generated Idealization
learningObjectives: Create global and cut free-body diagrams.
gradingNotes: Do not show the instructor reference image before this modeling task.
student: Sketch a planar circular-arc cantilever of radius R and terminal angle θt. Show the fixed root, decreasing downward load q(θ), section S, and local tangent and normal directions. Draw both the whole-member and outboard-section free-body diagrams. Do not infer dimensions from the photograph.
instructor: A complete response shows x(θ)=R sinθ, y(θ)=R(1−cosθ), the fixed-root reactions, downward load per arc length, and at S the local axial, shear, and moment resultants on a clearly identified cut face.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State the scope of the teaching model.
student: State assumptions needed to reduce the exhibit to the assigned model and explain the slender-member stress approximation.
instructor: Assume a fixed planar root, circular-arc centerline, prismatic RHS, total static gravity load per arc length, linear elasticity, and small deformation. Use ordinary axial-plus-flexure stress because H/R is small; omit classical tight-radius curved-beam stress, torsion, deflection, local/lateral buckling, connection flexibility, detailed contacts, impact, fatigue, and fabrication effects.

title: Analysis Plan
student: Explain the solution sequence from centerline parameterization through the engineering recommendation.
instructor: Parameterize the arc, integrate load and moment for root reactions, cut at S and integrate the outboard load, resolve the cut force into local axes, compute section properties and combined normal stress, then compare the governing stress with the yield criterion and discuss limitations.

title: Arc Geometry
student: Using s=Rθ, x(θ)=Rsinθ, and y(θ)=R(1−cosθ), determine the arc length, tip coordinates, and coordinates of S.

title: Total Load and Root Reactions
learningObjectives: Integrate load and moment on a curved centerline.
student: Write q(θ)=q0+(qt−q0)θ/θt. With ds=Rdθ, use W=R∫0θtq(θ)dθ and M0=R2∫0θtsinθ q(θ)dθ to find the total load and fixed-root reactions.
instructor: W = {{curved_tail_W_N}} N downward; H0 = {{curved_tail_H0_N}} N, V0 = {{curved_tail_V0_N}} N upward, and M0 = {{curved_tail_M0_Nm}} N·m counterclockwise.

title: Outboard Resultant Load
learningObjectives: Find the outboard resultant at S.
student: Isolate the segment from S to the tip and evaluate WS=R∫θSθtq(θ)dθ. State the direction of the cut force on the outboard free body.
instructor: WS = {{curved_tail_WS_N}} N downward, so the cut force on the outboard free body is equal and opposite: upward.

title: Local Axial and Shear Resultants
learningObjectives: Resolve the section force into local axes.
student: Using et=(cosθ,sinθ) and en=(−sinθ,cosθ), resolve the section force at S. Report axial force with tension positive on the left segment and report the shear magnitude.
instructor: On the left-segment sign convention, NS = {{curved_tail_NS_N}} N (compression); shear magnitude |VS| = {{curved_tail_VS_N}} N.

title: Section Moment
learningObjectives: Integrate the outboard moment about S.

title: Combined Normal Stress and Yield Margin
learningObjectives: Calculate slender-member normal stresses and yield margin.
student: Use t={{curved_tail_t_factor}}tnom, A=BH−(B−2t)(H−2t), and I=[BH3−(B−2t)(H−2t)3]/12. At S use the conservative magnitude |σ|=|N|/A+|M|(H/2)/I. Calculate the root stress, identify the controlling location, and compute n=Fy/|σ|governing.
instructor: t = {{curved_tail_t_mm}} mm, A = {{curved_tail_A_mm2}} mm², I = {{curved_tail_I_mm4}} mm⁴. At S: |σa| = {{curved_tail_sigma_axial_S_MPa}} MPa, |σb| = {{curved_tail_sigma_bending_S_MPa}} MPa, conservative |σS| = {{curved_tail_sigma_S_MPa}} MPa. Root stress = {{curved_tail_sigma_root_MPa}} MPa. {{curved_tail_governing_location}} governs at {{curved_tail_sigma_governing_MPa}} MPa; nmin = {{curved_tail_n_min}} — {{curved_tail_strength_check}}.

title: Engineering Assessment
student: Recommend whether the preliminary armature meets the assigned yield criterion. Explain why the slender-member approximation is reasonable, and identify at least four important checks omitted from this classroom model. Do not present the result as certification of a museum installation.
